verdict: folder-sync with push sync is the fastest networked tool measured in four of five directions (machine→machine 390 ms, web paths 286–328 ms, agent 327 ms, 1 KB p50), 3–5× ahead of the only off-the-shelf tool with a web copy. It still loses offline catch-up after a network drop, and every configuration makes false conflict copies on a save storm. All of this is on branch lane/sync-bench, not merged.
verdict_points: Measured, not tabled: 2 machines + a web host + an agent, each machine behind its own proxy, on this computer; 10 trials per cell at random phases, sha256 on every arrival. Five off-the-shelf tools ran on the same workloads from checksummed official binaries.

Off the shelf, nothing beats it on a network hop: Unison 515 ms, lsyncd tuned 1.06 s, Syncthing 1.38 s at its fastest watcher setting (8.4 s by default), rclone bisync 1.5 s. Only Mutagen is faster (40 ms), and only because its local session has no network at all.

Web and agent: rclone bisync is the only off-the-shelf tool with a cloud copy. It is 3–5× slower (m2w 1.47 s, w2m 1.75 s, m2a 1.28 s) and would cost about $332/month on R2 at Zach's scale (modelled), against folder-sync's $5.67. It also lost the final save in 3 of 10 storms.

The one loss is catch-up after a network drop. Push's hub reconnect backoff (0.5 s doubling to a 30 s cap) made it 19.2 s, worse than polling's 9.4 s. A 1 s cap brings it to 0.65 s (Unison supervised 118 ms, lsyncd 213 ms). The sweep below has every point.

A correctness bug the bench found: on the save storm (20 saves 50 ms apart), the receiving machine sometimes logs “edited here, but it is <host>'s file” and parks a false conflict copy. The final bytes are always right (0 lost writes, 0 bad hashes in every folder-sync cell). It happens in every configuration, polling included, and most often on today's v0 head: 10 of 10 web storms.
optimized:
debounce 50 ms · hub reconnect cap 1 s · safety-net poll 300 s (lane/fast-sync + bench/fast/patches/fast-sync-tunables.patch; defaults are 100 ms, 30 s, 60 s). Confirmed end to end on the full small matrix (sw-push-optimal):

  • m2m 390 ms · m2w 328 ms · w2m 286 ms · m2a 327 ms · offline drop 652 ms (was 19.2 s) · offline sleep 265 ms (p50s, 1 KB)
  • Idle per machine: 0.062 % CPU (bound 0.1 %; push's default 60 s poll is 0.36 %), 161 wakeups/min (bound 300), 1.9 KB/min (bound 10 KB)
  • Cost: $5.67/month modelled, $0.67 over the $5 Workers Paid bound; all of it is R2 class B reads (11.8M against 10M free) under the pessimistic “every change read by all 14 other devices” assumption
  • Per constraint: C2 idle CPU, C3 bandwidth and C4 wakeups are met. C1 cost misses by $0.67 (modelled). C5 correctness is not met, because of the storm false conflict (2 copies in 40 storm trials), which no setting fixes.

Rejected settings:

  • A 25 ms or 1 ms debounce is 20–40 ms faster but triggered the storm race most often (20 conflict copies in the 25 ms best-combination run). 50 ms was the only debounce with a clean sweep point.
  • A 15 s safety poll costs more idle CPU (0.50 %) for nothing.
  • Poll at 1–2 s gets m2w and w2m under 1.4 s, but at 2.3–4.5 % of a core idle and $19–32/month.
method_limits: Every host runs on one machine over loopback, so there is no WAN round trip; real use adds the same RTTs to every networked tool. Rows say env: local-loopback.

The machine was shared with other work. Each row records load1, and push's baseline ran at load 20–50. Its m2w 1 KB p95 of 4.6 s is that noise: the identical code with tuned settings ran at load 3–5 and gave 436 ms.
Real R2 was not run: Zach's account is over its 1 GiB quota (403 over_quota at the first PUT).
Cost is modelled from measured request rates. The hub's Durable Object load is not observable locally, so the fast-sync report's pessimistic 151k requests/month is used.
Wakeups count context switches of processes alive at the end of each window, a battery proxy that undercounts short-lived rclone runs (poll most).
Mutagen ran local-to-local in one daemon (no network, no drop fault), so it is shown but excluded from the competitiveness ratio.
Unison “supervised” (client restarted every 1 s) is a bench preset: bare Unison never recovered from a drop (10/10 timed out). lsyncd is one-way A→B.
200 MB through the web host is refused by design (413: the web host takes files up to 32 MiB), so those cells are errors, not timeouts.
A 100-file burst through the web host is slow in every folder-sync variant (m2w 10.7 s, w2m 15 s, against about 2 s machine to machine). The path is untuned, and the bench shows it.
